title: China Denies AI Tool Use in South Korean Bank Hacks
summary:
A 26 year old man accused of orchestrating cyberattacks on the financial sector in Seoul now claims he was framed and is actually employed at a convenience store in Henan. Beijing's Foreign Ministry separately warned that accusations of a domestic operator utilizing AI to steal banking data may be based on 'politically motivated misinformation,' stating that the Chinese government does not know the specifics of the intrusions.

The intrusions targeted 7 financial institutions, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin and Hana Bank, and leaked data from about 68,000 customers. CrowdStrike identified the attacks as some of the first AI powered entries into the global financial system, attributing them to an operator using the open source ARTEX agent with DeepSeek v4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 models. President Lee Jae Myung ordered a full investigation after the suspect was reportedly unmasked by leaving public access to his own Claude Code sessions and a professional résumé.

selectedTweets.text:
🚨BREAKING: China's Foreign Ministry has now responded to CrowdStrike's report linking the South Korean bank hacks to a likely China-based operator using AI tools.

Beijing says it does not know the specifics, opposes hacking, and warns against "politically motivated misinformation."

CrowdStrike found the attacker used ARTEX powered by DeepSeek v4.1-Flash, alongside GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 in Claude Code sessions.

Exposed logs pointed to a 26-year-old in Guangdong, China. But the man linked to those details now claims he actually works at a convenience store in Henan and was FRAMED by someone else.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
🚨HOLY MOLY. A hacker suspected of attacking South Korean banks may have accidentally unmasked himself in the most ridiculous way: asking Claude Code to write a résumé highlighting his own hacking operations, complete with his personal details.

CrowdStrike traced the attacks to infrastructure running an AI hacking tool called ARTEX. Investigators then discovered publicly exposed folders on another server containing the hacker's saved Claude Code conversations.

In one chat, he asked Claude to write a cybersecurity résumé describing his ARTEX activities, supplying his phone number, Telegram handle, claimed age of 26, university and location in China. The same Telegram handle appeared in other hacking-related sessions.

He had also asked Claude where stolen Korean data is typically sold. His identity remains unconfirmed.
